answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with randomized live audits. Each identity must periodically pass an unpredictable, time-boxed interactive challenge: solve a fresh problem and answer follow-ups in real time. One operator running many faces cannot staff simultaneous audits, so failures cluster like a vine, exposing shared timing patterns. A failed identity's vault of earnings freezes, and it is exiled to a tundra of low-trust work until a harder re-audit passes. The attacker's cost is live attention per identity per audit, not a one-time purchase like cheap account creation.
